verify-before-using-ledger-facts.text: The client accepts a commitment under its own policy and checks the intended NFT state. Changed bytes, identity, root or network must never become accepted facts.

Replacing the data provider must preserve the accepted claim when evidence agrees. A provider cannot substitute its own root for the accepted anchor, and membership alone must not be treated as query completeness.

keep-dependent-reads-coherent.text: Reads and pagination remain at one selected state while new blocks arrive. Unavailable and expired chainpoints are refused. Fork behavior remains to be decided.

run-an-anchor-and-buy-ledger-capacity.text: An operator runs its own node and anchor for maximum trust independence, then buys archive access, retained views and proof generation. The terminal rejects evidence that does not verify against locally established roots. Validation and commitment maintenance remain local responsibilities.

observe-institutional-publications.text: An operator selects institutional publishers and verifies their signed roots. Unknown keys, wrong networks, incompatible schemes or unacceptable freshness must not establish accepted roots. This reduces local infrastructure with explicit institutional trust. No actual institutional participation is claimed.

buy-availability-and-switch-providers.text: An application buys observable coverage, retention, throughput, latency and uptime. It can switch to a compatible provider at the same chainpoint without changing anchor policy, using a new provider-local session. Unavailable views and history must be reported. Fallback must not silently change the root, chainpoint or strength of evidence.

add-an-application-without-another-chain.text: An application reconstructs state from transactions and historical inputs. Its result must match the authenticated application root. Missing history is a failure, not an empty successful answer.

delegate-proof-construction.text: The terminal may delegate proof construction to an untrusted application service or construct locally. Either way it checks the required claim against the authenticated application root. Wrong NFTs, substitute roots, invalid proofs and missing evidence must not be accepted. Nested root chains require a separate verified link at each step.

publish-trust-without-serving-queries.text: An anchor runs a node and computes signed commitments for each block. It does not have to retain historical query views. No institution is assumed to provide this service.

act-on-verified-facts.text: A terminal verifies the facts needed for its application, then builds a transaction or drives an external effect. Its application policy authorizes that action; a proof alone is not an instruction to act.

Ledger proofs are checked off-chain and are not placed in transaction redeemers. Application proofs are placed in redeemers. Cardano checks actual ledger validity, and application validators check the application proofs.

evidence-status.text: These stories are acceptance targets. No formal model, simulator or production conformance result has yet been delivered.
